title: In a first, scientists want to make exotic nuclei that contain only neutrons
content: A collaborative effort between researchers at the RIKEN Nishina Center for Accelerator-Based Science in Japan and the Institute for Basic Science (IBS) in South Korea is working to build exotic nuclei containing only neutrons. This groundbreaking work, known as ‘atomic number zero,’ has long been thought to be impossible by nuclear physicists. At the core of all matter are atoms, and at the core of the atom is its nucleus. Atomic nuclei contain nucleons, which are protons and neutrons. Positively charged protons determine the atomic number of the atom, while neutrally charged neutrons help in keeping the same-charge-bearing protons together. Interestingly, though, neutrons are unstable on their own. When left free, they undergo beta decay and transform into a proton. Yet, they remain important in the course of the formation of the universe, where they helped produce helium after the Big Bang as well as elements heavier than iron. Why look for pure neutron matter? Neutron stars are mostly composed of neutrons and are extremely dense objects, holding millions of tons of mass in spaces as small as a sugar cube. Nuclear physicists have not yet solved the puzzle of why neutron stars do not collapse into black holes. To examine this, they need to make a nuclei composed entirely of neutrons. Physicists believe that critical to solving this puzzle is the understanding of the three-neutron force, which emerges when three neutrons interact at once. Using heavy-ion beams accelerated at speeds nearly half the speed of light and directed at helium or hydrogen targets, researchers at RIKEN generated multineutron systems between 2016 and 2022. Conventional detectors work using electromagnetic interactions between particles. Since neutrally charged neutrons do not participate in these interactions, it is difficult to detect them. To determine whether the multineutron system formed, researchers had to reconstruct the missing mass from the reaction products. RIKEN experiments used the NEBULA neutron detector for this work. When neutron-rich nuclei collide with hydrogen nuclei, the trajectories and signals of recoil protons are used to determine the energies and positions of the neutrons. However, since neutron-proton interactions are rare, the efficiency of the detector remains as low as 0.1 percent. How Korean collaboration helpedRIKEN’s previous collaboration with the French research group worked to double the depth of the detector to 18.88 inches (48 cm). However, this could only help increase the efficiency to a little above one percent. The team got in touch with researchers at Institute for Basic Science (IBS) in South Korea who were building the ROAN accelerator and had finished constructing their neutron detector, dubbed LAMPS-NDA, boasting a depth of 31.5 inches (80 cm). After multiple meetings, the detector was moved to RIKEN and integrated into the existing detector system in May 2026.With the new detector on board, the detection efficiency at RIKEN for the four-neutron system nearly doubled to 3.5 percent. “Our goal is to create, for the first time on Earth, matter composed almost entirely of neutrons, similar to the material found inside neutron stars,” said Tomohiro Uesaka, Group Director of Nuclear Dynamics Research Group at RIKEN in a press release. “With detection efficiencies at this level, we have good reasons to expect meaningful results. Better detection efficiency also greatly increases our motivation for the experiment.”

title: China rolls out giant 328-foot support ship carrying 165-US-ton crane
content: A massive 328-foot (100-meter) offshore construction ship equipped with hybrid batteries, two underground vehicles, and a 165-US-ton (150-ton) lifting crane has been launched at a Chinese shipyard.Known as Echo, the giant vessel was being developed for Allseas, a Swiss offshore engineering company, at Wuchang Shipbuilding Industry Group’s shipyard in the city of Wuhan, China. It is the first of two sister vessels intended to expand the firm’s offshore operations.The second vessel, named Pulse, is under construction at the same shipyard. Both ships will support a broad range of operations. These include subsea construction, maintenance, decommissioning, and underwater inspections. They will also free up larger vessels in Allseas’ fleet to handle heavier construction projects. Echo’s launch took place on Tuesday, November 17. “The milestone was marked with a traditional launch ceremony attended by project team members and guests,” Allseas representatives said. A four-hour launchAccording to Allseas, Echo entered the water from the shipyard’s side-launch platform after several months of hull assembly and equipment installation. The carefully controlled operation took about four hours and included a temporary pause to check the vessel’s watertight integrity.However, despite the successful launch, the ship is not yet ready to enter service. It will remain at the Chinese shipyard, where the engineering team will complete the remaining commissioning activities.Before the official handover, the shipyard will test the vessel’s onboard equipment and systems to ensure they work properly. Allseas is expected to receive Echo in the fourth quarter of 2026. Pulse is scheduled to follow in the first quarter of 2027.Allseas’ offshore construction vessel Echo.Credit: Allseas / YouTube ScreenshotBoth ships are based on the SALT 308 offshore construction vessel design and will have the same equipment. In addition, each vessel will measure roughly 328 feet (100 meters) long and 75 feet (23 meters) wide.They will also have a cargo deck covering approximately 11,840 square feet (1,100 square meters) and accommodate up to 110 people. “This investment ensures Allseas remains at the forefront of the growing offshore construction and subsea installation sectors,” the company added. Hybrid batteries and ROVs Both vessels will include a 165-US-ton (150-ton) active heave-compensated crane. This is an offshore crane that can keep a lifted load stable vertically despite wave-induced motion. It prevents slack cables, shock loads, and unintended load movement during subsea installations, offshore wind maintenance, and marine construction.Meanwhile, the ships will carry two work-class remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) in a dedicated hangar. These submersible robots will support subsea construction, inspections, repair activities, and maintenance.At the same time, a hybrid battery with a total capacity of 1,500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) will also be installed onboard the vessels. Both ships will have propulsion systems prepared for methanol, meaning they could use it as an alternative fuel. DP2 dynamic positioning technology will automatically keep both ships in place and facing the right direction without the need for anchors. This is particularly useful during construction, where precise positioning is essential.According to Allseas, the new ships will allow the company to work on several projects at the same time. “The two vessels are based on the same design and equipment configuration and will together expand Allseas’ capacity for subsea construction and support activities around the world,” the firm concluded in a press release.

title: GENTO's 21-DoF robot hand takes on backlash, fragility and weak grip
content: Robot hands have become one of the busiest corners of humanoid robotics. In recent months, companies have taken very different routes toward useful dexterity, from Boston Dynamics’ four-finger, 13-DoF hand for Atlas to 1X’s 25-DoF tendon-driven hands for NEO.GENTO, an independent humanoid robot brand incubated by Tianji Intelligence, has now put its own design on the table.GENTO showed its 21-degree-of-freedom (DoF) dexterous-hand prototype for the first time at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). The hand was on static display at GENTO’s Booth 602 at the JW Marriott Austin.Rather than leading with a single headline figure, GENTO built the hand around four mechanical problems that tend to show up together in dexterous hands. These are backlash, damage from impacts and overloads, joints that resist being pushed back, and weak fingertip force in small fingers.Where the 21 degrees goThe prototype has five active degrees of freedom in the thumb and four in each of the other four fingers, giving the thumb one more degree of freedom than each of the fingers.According to the product specifications, the hand weighs 750 g (1.65 lb) excluding cables and measures 200 × 96 × 45 mm (7.9 × 3.8 × 1.8 in).It has a maximum grasp diameter of 100 mm (3.9 in), a rated fingertip force of 10 N, and a minimum opening and closing time of 0.5 seconds.Repeat positioning accuracy is ±0.05 mm. The hand connects over industrial Ethernet and runs on DC 36–60 V.Four problems, one linkage designThe first problem is backlash, the small amount of slack in a transmission that lets a finger drift from where it was told to go. GENTO uses a high-precision, low-clearance linkage transmission to reduce that play.The second is fragility. Hands often take the first knock when a robot meets a table edge or an unexpected object, so GENTO designed the transmission to withstand impacts and overloads. GENTO specifies a no-load grasping life of one million cycles.The third is backdrivability. Every joint in the hand can be moved by an external force, which means a finger can give way on contact instead of fighting it.GENTO pairs that mechanical compliance with MIT force and position hybrid control, so the hand can manage both where the fingers go and how hard they press.The fourth is grip strength. Small fingers leave little room for actuators, so GENTO uses an efficient linkage mechanism designed to deliver more rated fingertip force within the same finger dimensions.GENTO says the aim was to address precision, durability, backdrivability and gripping force within the same design, rather than solving each problem on its own.Built on a force-sensing stackThe hand is the top layer of what Tianji Intelligence describes as a five-tier product stack. It starts with MEMS joint torque sensors, moves up through integrated joint modules and TIANJI-branded force-controlled dual arms, and continues to GENTO’s whole-body force-controlled systems.Tianji Intelligence began developing its MEMS torque sensors in 2015. On its core arm platforms, the company reports a minimum detectable torque of 0.02 N·m and a torque-loop bandwidth of 160 Hz.TIANJI Marvin Pro and GENTO Luna at CoRL 2026. Image courtesy of GENTO.Two platforms ran live at the booth. GENTO Luna, a wheeled, foldable humanoid robot fitted with GENTO’s in-house dexterous hands, took part in a teleoperated “Mirror & High-Five” demonstration.Under an operator’s control, Luna waved, made heart gestures, and exchanged high-fives with visitors. It then picked up a pen box from a nearby table and handed it over.TIANJI Marvin Pro, a fixed-base dual-arm platform, took spoken English instructions from visitors and then recognized, selected, and grasped the requested object, such as a pen box or a plush toy.A TIANJI platform in NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 demosIn his CoRL keynote on Nov. 9, NVIDIA’s Jim Fan introduced GR00T 2, an open-world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. The model predicts future video frames and robot actions together and can transfer skills learned from human demonstrations to robots.The launch demonstrations used a TIANJI Marvin Pro platform, built for NVIDIA by Tianji Intelligence with a tailored head and body.In one example, NVIDIA researchers recorded human hand movements with a wearable exoskeleton. GR00T 2 then ran on TIANJI Marvin Pro, fitted with two dexterous hands, to prepare banana yogurt. NVIDIA’s published research demonstrations also include the platform scooping granola.A TIANJI Marvin Pro platform performs two-handed manipulation in NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 demonstration video. Image courtesy of GENTO and Tianji Intelligence.From industrial robots to humanoidsTianji Intelligence was founded in Shenzhen in 2015 as an industrial robotics and motion-control company, incubated by Yaskawa Electric and Everwin Precision. It has delivered more than 30,000 industrial robots.The company moved into force-controlled humanoid arms in 2023 and 2024. It reports delivering more than 2,000 of those arms within four months in 2025 and holding production or supply relationships with more than 45 robot manufacturers and embodied-AI companies.In May 2026, Tianji Intelligence raised RMB 1 billion in Series B and B+ funding from investors including Hillhouse Ventures and Meituan, followed by a strategic Series B++ round in September with Ant Group and Sofina.CoRL 2026 was GENTO’s first appearance at the conference, following its global debut at ICRA 2026 in Vienna. GENTO robots have also arrived at the APEC China 2026 venue in Shenzhen, where they are scheduled to provide services during the meetings.The hand remains a prototype, and GENTO has not announced pricing or availability. More information is available on the GENTO website.About GENTOGENTO is an independent humanoid robot brand incubated by Tianji Intelligence. Its portfolio includes humanoid robot systems (GENTO Luna and GENTO Skye) and the proprietary 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand. Its humanoid systems incorporate Tianji Intelligence’s TIANJI-branded force-controlled arms. GENTO draws on Tianji Intelligence’s work in MEMS torque sensing, integrated joints, compliant control, teleoperation, and data systems, together with customer application experience, to support robotics development and physical interaction. Learn more at www.gentorobotics.ai.

title: Argonne unleashes supercomputer with 2,688 NVIDIA chips to automate scientific discovery
content: Argonne National Laboratory’s Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF) is expanding its inference service, led by the deployment of a new large-scale system called Tara, built on supercomputing architecture. The expansion brings a wider array of AI/super intelligence (SI) models and agentic workflows directly into scientific research.The upgrade arrives at a pivotal moment for American science. Going beyond simple prompts, researchers can now use autonomous AI agents to plan experiments, write code, and run lab instruments at scale.“The ALCF has long provided the computing resources researchers need to pursue science at scale,” said Venkat Vishwanath, SI team lead at the ALCF. ​“As inference and agentic workflows take on a growing role in science, we are evolving to provide new services and tools that complement our computing systems and help scientists be more productive in their research.”Advancement in memory and speedTara is a powerhouse built alongside Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) on its exascale-class HPE Cray Supercomputing EX4000 architecture. The supercomputer packs 672 computing nodes and 2,688 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips. Tara delivers roughly 100 times the GPU memory previously available on the platform.Tara does not stand alone. Argonne also unveiled Minerva, an eight-node system built with World Wide Technology and powered by 64 NVIDIA B200 GPUs. At the same time, the lab tripled its Metis platform to six SambaRacks equipped with 96 SambaNova SN40L chips.Paired with the existing Sophia platform, this hardware expansion supports more than 50 advanced models, including open-weight large language models, scientific foundation models, and computer vision tools. All of these capabilities operate inside a secure, on-premises environment built to safeguard sensitive research data.Real-world science in motionOffering inference as a shared national resource gives individual research teams affordable access to massive AI models via APIs or a chat-like interface. These scientific agents connect directly to supercomputing power and specialized tools to prepare simulations, optimize code, and analyze experimental data in real time.“We’re moving to a point where agentic workflows are playing a much bigger role in the scientific process,” said ALCF Director of Science Katherine Riley. ​“We’re seeing researchers put agents to work to connect scientific tools, automate multistep calculations and data analysis, and use experimental results to help determine what to investigate next.”Early applications already show how this infrastructure accelerates the Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Genesis Mission for discovery science, national security, and energy innovation. Argonne’s ChemGraph framework turns plain descriptions of chemistry and materials problems into automated simulations and analyses.Meanwhile, the SYNAPS-I project demonstrated autonomous experiments at a DOE light source, where an AI agent scanned a microelectronics sample, analyzed the visuals with computer vision models, and steered the instrument directly to a target boundary.For scientists across the ALCF user community and DOE national laboratories, the limiting factor is shifting from access to raw computing power to imagination.Vishwanath highlighted the payoff of embedding inference directly into simulations and experiments. Researchers can now tackle far larger problems and move from an initial spark of an idea to a breakthrough faster than ever before.

title: Lockheed Martin’s 300kW laser takes down cruise missile in first test
content: Lockheed Martin’s 300-kilowatt Valkyrie laser has destroyed a target standing in for a cruise missile for the first time, a company executive said. Lockheed developed the high-energy laser for the US Army, which had already dropped plans to put the system into service when the company disclosed the result.Jack Cheung, program director for Lockheed Martin’s Laser and Sensor Systems, announced the test on social media. He said the team destroyed the target without additional tracking aids, but gave no date, location, or distance for the test.Valkyrie takes on a cruise missile targetCheung called the test the team’s “FIRST EVER engagement against a surrogate cruise missile target – with full kill chain integration.” The announcement gave no details about the surrogate itself or the conditions under which it flew.“It was the first kill WITHOUT track augmentation, WITH short engagement time at meaningful distance,” Cheung wrote. In this context, track augmentation means adding equipment to a test target, such as a beacon or reflector, to help the system follow it.He did not specify how long the engagement lasted. A Lockheed Martin spokesperson confirmed to Laser Wars that the weapon used in the test was the Indirect Fire Protection Capability–High Energy Laser, or IFPC-HEL, also known as Valkyrie.A photograph accompanying the announcement showed the system beside a military truck outside a hangar. The laser’s beam director sat atop a tan enclosure about the size of a shipping container.The Army drops plans to field ValkyrieValkyrie is among the highest-powered lasers the US military has tested. The Army commissioned the system to help defend troops and bases against several kinds of airborne threats, including cruise missiles, drones, rockets, and mortar rounds.A March 9 Congressional Research Service report said Army officials no longer planned to move IFPC-HEL into active service, according to Laser Wars. The system still appeared at a directed-energy demonstration in June at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. Valkyrie was one of several laser weapons shown to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the event.The New Mexico event was a military demonstration of the system. Cheung’s announcement did not identify White Sands as the location of the cruise missile test.The Army and Navy pursue a joint laserThe Pentagon’s fiscal 2027 budget request said the military would apply lessons from IFPC-HEL to the Joint Laser Weapon System, a development effort involving both the Army and Navy, Laser Wars reported. Defeating cruise missiles is among the goals of the joint program.In July, the Pentagon awarded Lockheed Martin and nLight contracts worth a combined $86 million under the program. Laser Wars reported that the awards carried a ceiling of $847 million.The contracts cover development work on laser weapons capable of defeating cruise missiles, the same class of threat represented by the target in Valkyrie’s test.“Huge congratulations to the entire team that is working to get directed energy into the hands of operators who need it!” Cheung wrote. The joint program gives the Army and Navy a way to carry forward work from the Valkyrie program as they develop a laser for that role.

title: 151 humanoid robots dance in sync to break Guinness World Record
content: China has set a new Guinness World Record after 151 humanoid robots performed a synchronized dance routine in Shenzhen. The record-setting performance took place on November 17, ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting scheduled for November 18–19 in the southern Chinese technology hub.The robots completed the challenge for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously within one hour. The event exceeded its initial target of 110 robots, with Guinness World Records adjudicator Xiong Wen announcing that all 151 machines had completed the performance.Humanoids synchronize movesThe Shenzhen Longgang District Artificial Intelligence (Robotics) Bureau led the event and organized it with a robot 6S store, ENGINEAI Robotics Technology, and other robotics companies.ENGINEAI’s full-size T800 humanoid robots played a key role in the demonstration, with 20 units showcasing the company’s swarm-control capabilities. Groups of Unitree G1 and AGIBOT X2 humanoids also participated in the performance.The T800 is a full-size humanoid robot measuring 1.73 meters (5.7 feet) tall and weighing approximately 75 kilograms (165 pounds). According to ENGINEAI, the machine features a high-torque output of 450 newton-meters, allowing it to perform demanding movements that require considerable balance and joint strength. These include spinning kicks, rising dragon punches, kip-ups, and backflip landings, reports Gasgoo. The robot’s ability to perform dynamic movements makes it suitable for demonstrations involving coordinated motion and physical agility. However, the Shenzhen performance also highlighted another important aspect of humanoid robotics: coordinating large numbers of machines to perform the same movements at the same time.Synchronizing multiple humanoid robots requires coordination across their motion-control systems, joint movements, and timing. Maintaining consistent movements across a large group also presents challenges involving stability and the execution of programmed routines.Humanoids welcome APECThe record attempt formed part of a broader effort to showcase Shenzhen’s robotics industry ahead of the APEC summit.During the summit period, ENGINEAI’s T800 and PM01 humanoid robots also participated in several events, demonstrating applications involving entertainment performances, reception services, and smart traffic management.Other robotics companies also brought their machines to public demonstrations across the city. Reports from Shenzhen showed humanoid robots performing synchronized dances, martial arts routines, and other interactive demonstrations for residents and visitors.The city has become an important center for China’s technology industry, hosting major companies such as Huawei, Tencent, BYD, and DJI. Its robotics ecosystem includes developers of industrial automation systems, service robots, and humanoid machines.The APEC gathering brings together 21 member economies representing approximately 60 percent of global economic output. Hosting the meeting allows China to present Shenzhen as a center for technological development and advanced manufacturing.The 151-robot performance was therefore more than an entertainment spectacle. It demonstrated how advances in robotics, motion control, and multi-machine coordination are increasingly being brought into public-facing applications.As humanoid robot developers work toward commercial deployment, demonstrations involving multiple machines could help showcase the potential of coordinated robotic systems in entertainment, manufacturing, and service environments.

title: Ford ships first US-made LFP cells for mainstream electric vehicles
content: Ford has started shipping its first lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells from a new Michigan factory, marking the automaker’s entry into battery manufacturing and a step toward producing more affordable electric vehicles in the US.The first prismatic cells have rolled off the production line at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan in Marshall. They are heading to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky, where they will power prototypes of the upcoming Fathom electric pickup.Ford says it will become the first company to deliver LFP batteries in the US for mainstream consumer automotive use. The milestone follows years of work to establish domestic production of a battery chemistry widely used by Chinese manufacturers.The Michigan facility is owned and operated by Ford, but its manufacturing technology is licensed from China’s Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL), the world’s largest electric vehicle battery maker.Lower-cost batteries for EVsFord selected LFP chemistry for its Universal Electric Vehicle Platform because it can help reduce battery costs without relying on nickel or cobalt. The chemistry also offers durability over years of charging and use, making it suitable for vehicles expected to support additional functions such as bidirectional home power.The automaker chose rectangular prismatic cells because they can fit directly into the vehicle’s chassis. Ford is also designing the battery pack as a structural component of the vehicle rather than simply housing it inside the frame.This approach is intended to reduce the number of parts, weight, and manufacturing complexity. Ford says the combination of cell design and vehicle architecture will help make its next generation of electric vehicles more affordable.The Fathom pickup will be the first vehicle built on the Universal Electric Vehicle Platform. Its prototypes will use the initial battery shipments from Michigan as engineers continue development.Production scales in MichiganBlueOval Battery Park Michigan’s assembly lines can produce 40 cells per minute, according to Ford, placing the facility among the fastest LFP prismatic battery production lines outside China. The company says the plant has additional capacity to increase output.Manufacturing speed is only part of the challenge. Ford is also using automated inspection systems, including image-recognition tools, to identify defects during production. The company aims to reduce defects to levels measured per billion cells rather than per million.The plant’s production expertise will also support Ford Energy’s planned battery energy storage business in Glendale, Kentucky. The company is preparing to manufacture battery storage systems for applications beyond electric vehicles.Ford plans to bring a separate battery pack facility in Marshall online in 2027, ahead of the Fathom’s launch. The first cells will help inform prototype development and the next stages of production preparation.The launch comes as automakers seek lower-cost battery technologies to make electric vehicles more competitive. LFP batteries have gained ground because they avoid expensive nickel and cobalt while offering long service life.For Ford, the Michigan operation also represents an effort to build domestic manufacturing expertise while relying on licensed technology from an established Chinese supplier. The first shipments mark a shift from factory construction and trial production to supplying cells for vehicle development.

title: Rolls-Royce SMR tests new component to protect plants from earthquakes
content: Rolls-Royce SMR has completed an important construction test for its small modular reactor (SMR) program. A new precast concrete component could help make future nuclear plants easier to manufacture and assemble.Skanska built and tested an aseismic bearing pedestal at its Bentley Works facility in Doncaster, England. The demonstrator validates an off-site manufacturing approach for a component that plays a crucial role in protecting nuclear infrastructure during earthquakes.The achievement gives Rolls-Royce SMR another construction method to evaluate before deploying its factory-built reactor design. It also demonstrates how conventional construction techniques could support the industrial-scale production of nuclear power plants.Testing earthquake protectionAseismic bearing pedestals support isolation devices within the Rolls-Royce SMR design. These devices help separate buildings and other structures from ground movement during seismic events.The isolation system reduces the forces that earthquakes can transfer into critical infrastructure. Its performance therefore plays an important role in protecting the reactor facility and supporting its structural resilience.Skanska’s demonstrator allowed engineers to test the manufacturing approach before committing to full-scale deployment. Producing the component away from the construction site could also give manufacturers greater control over quality and production schedules.The prototype represents a first-of-its-kind precast bearing pedestal for the Rolls-Royce SMR design. Skanska completed its construction and technical trials at Bentley Works, bringing its engineering and manufacturing capabilities into the project.Factory production takes shapeOff-site manufacturing forms an important part of the Rolls-Royce SMR construction strategy. The company wants to move significant portions of plant construction into controlled manufacturing environments.That approach could reduce the amount of work required at individual construction sites. It could also improve consistency across multiple reactors by allowing suppliers to repeat established manufacturing processes.Rolls-Royce SMR Operations and Supply Chain Director Ruth Todd said the demonstrator supports the company’s plans for factory-built nuclear plants. She also pointed to the importance of testing critical components before deployment.Early cooperation with suppliers helps engineers identify potential problems before construction begins. It also gives manufacturers time to refine their processes ahead of larger production requirements.Skanska UK Executive Vice President Terry Muckian highlighted the engineering work behind the demonstrator. The project combined the contractor’s civil engineering, design and steelwork manufacturing experience.UK nuclear plans advanceRolls-Royce SMR has secured a place in the UK’s small modular reactor deployment program through Great British Energy – Nuclear. The country’s first planned deployment will take place at Wylfa on Anglesey, North Wales.The UK expects the site to generate its first electricity in the mid-2030s. The Czech Republic and Sweden also feature in the company’s international deployment plans.Small modular reactors use factory-manufactured sections that engineers assemble at their final locations. This approach aims to make nuclear construction more repeatable than conventional projects.The bearing pedestal demonstrator addresses one part of that challenge. Its successful trials give Rolls-Royce SMR and Skanska a tested manufacturing approach for a component that supports seismic protection.Further engineering and manufacturing work will determine how the method translates into future plant construction. The broader objective remains consistent production across a fleet of reactors.

title: US plant makes battery-grade graphite from natural gas for first time
content: A US startup has begun operating what it describes as the world’s first plant to produce battery-grade graphite from natural gas, opening a new route to manufacturing a critical material used in electric vehicle batteries.Molten Industries commissioned its demonstration facility in Oakland, California, on November 18. The plant uses methane pyrolysis to convert natural gas into graphite and hydrogen, potentially creating a domestic alternative to conventional graphite production.The facility has an annual production capacity of 300 metric tons of graphite anode material. It uses a single modular reactor, with the company reporting natural gas-to-graphite yields above 95 percent.Graphite is a key component of lithium-ion batteries, forming the anode that stores and releases electrical charge. It is widely used in electric vehicles, grid storage systems, and consumer electronics.The US remains heavily dependent on overseas suppliers for battery-grade graphite. China controls around 75 percent of the global graphite anode supply chain and 97 percent of synthetic graphite anode production, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence figures cited by TechCrunch.Splitting methane into materialsMolten’s process uses methane, the main component of natural gas, as its feedstock. Instead of burning the gas, the technology heats it without oxygen, separating its carbon and hydrogen components.The carbon is processed into graphite suitable for battery anodes, while the hydrogen can be used in industrial applications such as fertilizer production, petroleum refining, methanol manufacturing, and steelmaking.The company says its process uses four times cheaper feedstock and three times less electricity than conventional synthetic graphite production. It also claims the technology eliminates the need for a graphitization furnace, which is used to convert carbon materials into highly crystalline graphite.Molten uses electrical resistive heating to drive the reaction. The company says the process produces no direct process emissions because methane is split without combustion.However, this does not mean the entire production chain is emissions-free. Emissions associated with natural gas extraction, transportation, and electricity generation would still need to be considered when assessing its overall environmental footprint.Scaling domestic graphite supplyThe Oakland plant is intended to demonstrate that the technology can operate continuously and provide a modular blueprint for larger facilities.According to TechCrunch, the plant’s annual output could supply enough graphite for around 300 megawatt-hours of batteries, equivalent to approximately 4,300 electric vehicles. Most of its production will go to undisclosed customers testing the material in battery cells.That customer validation will be important in determining whether the graphite can meet manufacturers’ requirements for battery performance and consistency.Molten also plans to make samples of its MG Series battery-anode graphite available from December 1, 2026. The company has not announced details of its next production facility, although it says future plants will build on the Oakland reactor design.The technology builds on more than a century of research into methane decomposition. Splitting natural gas into carbon and hydrogen was patented in the late 19th century, but producing high-quality graphite through the process has remained a challenge.Molten’s demonstration plant marks a step toward commercializing that approach. Whether it can compete with established graphite producers will depend on scaling production, proving material quality, and demonstrating competitive costs.

title: China's Long March 2D rocket sends mystery satellite into orbit
content: China has sent another experimental spacecraft into orbit, adding a relatively mysterious satellite to its growing fleet of technology-testing missions. A Long March 2D rocket carried Shijian-24 into a planned sun-synchronous orbit from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center on November 19.The rocket lifted off at 6:51 a.m. China Standard Time from Launch Complex 9 in Shanxi province. China confirmed that the spacecraft reached its intended orbit and declared the mission a complete success. The launch also marked the 678th flight of China’s Long March rocket family.Shijian-24’s unknown missionChina has not disclosed Shijian-24’s specific mission objectives or identified its manufacturer. The spacecraft’s designation offers some clues about its potential role, however.China uses the Shijian name for spacecraft that test technologies and establish operational procedures. The designation translates to “Practice” in English. Another category, Shiyan, identifies experimental spacecraft focused on technology development. These designations help distinguish different types of technology demonstration missions within China’s space program.Shijian-24 may also have considerable physical dimensions. Its Long March 2D rocket used a payload fairing measuring 3.8 meters in diameter. That enclosure protected the spacecraft during its journey through the atmosphere. The relatively wide fairing provides a useful indication of the payload envelope available for the mission.The satellite’s planned sun-synchronous orbit could support missions requiring consistent lighting conditions. Such orbits prove useful for Earth observation and other applications. However, China has not confirmed whether Shijian-24 will perform either function.The spacecraft joins a relatively small group of Shijian missions launched this year. China previously placed Shijian-31 into a highly elliptical orbit in June. An earlier attempt involving Shijian-32 ended in a launch failure in January.China also expanded its Shiyan fleet in March. Two Shiyan-30 satellites entered orbit alongside the less-documented Shiyan-33 spacecraft. Their missions further demonstrate China’s interest in testing new spacecraft technologies through dedicated orbital platforms.Long March 2D handles coldThe November 19 mission also presented some additional ground-level challenges. Taiyuan’s cold weather required launch teams to modify their preparations for the Long March 2D.Engineers installed extra thermal insulation on the rocket before launch. The material separated harmlessly during the initial moments of flight. Ground crews also heated critical sections of the vehicle before liftoff.These preparations helped protect sensitive equipment and systems against low temperatures. Thermal management remains important during launch operations, particularly when vehicles face changing environmental conditions. Even relatively routine launches require adjustments when weather affects ground infrastructure and rocket hardware.Interestingly, this Long March 2D did not feature the hardware changes introduced on another vehicle a week earlier. That earlier rocket received flight computer improvements and design optimizations. Those changes included removing aerodynamic fins from the vehicle.China did not explain why the latest rocket lacked these modifications. Its older production batch may explain the difference, although officials have not confirmed that possibility.China’s expanding launch recordThe mission added another milestone to China’s increasingly busy launch calendar. It marked the 108th flight of the Long March 2D family.The Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, which develops the rocket, also recorded its 284th Long March mission. Its commercial launch vehicle subsidiary markets the Long March 2D.The rocket remains an established part of China’s orbital launch fleet. China has now conducted 82 orbital launch attempts in 2026. The latest mission adds another spacecraft to the country’s expanding satellite infrastructure.

title: US Marines set world's longest 187-mile troposcatter comms link
content: The U.S. Marine Corps has established its longest recorded low-power troposcatter communications link, spanning 187 miles across Hawaii. Comtech Telecommunications supplied the portable radio technology behind the demonstration during Exercise Tropo Thunder.The system connected Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on Oahu with the Pohakuloa Training Area on Hawaii’s Big Island. It maintained an average throughput of approximately 10 Mbps across the extended overwater route.More importantly, the demonstration showed how expeditionary forces can establish long-distance communications without satellite connections or fiber infrastructure. The setup also required relatively little power and a small deployment team.Portable radios extend military reachComtech’s COMET MPR system uses troposcatter technology to transmit signals beyond the conventional radio horizon. The technique relies on scattering radio waves through the troposphere, allowing distant ground stations to communicate.That capability offers military units another option when terrain or distance prevents conventional line-of-sight communications. It also provides an alternative when satellite connectivity becomes unavailable or unreliable.During the Hawaii exercise, the connection maintained 100 percent availability. Round-trip latency remained approximately 6 milliseconds throughout the demonstration.Those figures are particularly relevant for distributed military operations. Reliable connections allow personnel at separated locations to exchange information without depending on intermediate communications infrastructure.The system achieved these results using low transmit power at both ends of the link. Comtech did not disclose the individual transmission power levels.Deployment takes 30 minutesThe equipment’s physical footprint is another important part of the demonstration. Each MPR radio and its accompanying 2.4-meter inflatable antenna fits inside an airline-checkable case.Military personnel can transport the equipment without relying on specialized heavy-lift logistics. Once at the deployment site, crews can establish the field configuration in approximately 30 minutes.The complete setup operates on less than 350 watts of total prime power. That requirement reduces the electrical support needed to maintain long-distance terrestrial communications.Such characteristics could prove useful during island-hopping operations across the Pacific. Expeditionary units often operate across separated locations where permanent communications infrastructure remains limited.Comtech says its system gives military forces an additional beyond-line-of-sight communications pathway. It can complement existing networks without requiring satellites or intermediate ground stations.Marines explore resilient communicationsExercise Tropo Thunder also demonstrated the potential of modern low-power troposcatter equipment for smaller military formations. Traditional long-distance terrestrial communications systems often require substantial equipment and supporting infrastructure.Comtech’s approach packages that capability into equipment that a small team can transport and deploy. The demonstration offered the Marine Corps an opportunity to evaluate its performance across a challenging overwater route.“Exercise Tropo Thunder demonstrated just how far modern troposcatter communications have advanced,” said Mark Yamamoto, Comtech’s vice president of North America Solutions.He added that low-power troposcatter technology could help expeditionary forces maintain connectivity in demanding operational environments.The 187-mile result gives the Marine Corps another option for maintaining communications across geographically separated positions. It also demonstrates how portable terrestrial links could support military operations across the Pacific without constant satellite access.

title: Gemini 4 Neon brings 3x faster performance to complex coding tasks
content: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a new model designed to handle complex software engineering, scientific research, and enterprise workflows, claiming it can deliver performance comparable to its larger Gemini 4 Carbon model at three times the speed and 60 percent of the cost.The model is designed for long-running, multi-step tasks, including debugging large codebases, analyzing extensive datasets and coordinating multiple agents to complete complex projects.According to Google, Neon matched or exceeded Carbon in overall quality during early internal evaluations while completing tasks three times faster. The company also said the model has its lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing.Neon scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its highest xhigh thinking level, placing it third overall, according to Google’s reported results. It also ranked second on the Vals Index and the new Agent Arena Index for steerability, which measures how effectively a model adapts to user corrections during a task.Faster coding and researchSoftware engineering is a major focus of the release. Google said Neon ranked first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, scoring 58.6, and achieved 65.2 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.1.The model also scored 39 percent on SWE-sweep when tested within Google’s Antigravity environment, more than tripling its 12.8 percent result on the mini-SWE harness.These capabilities are intended to help developers work across multiple files, debug complex repositories, and make targeted changes without repeatedly processing the same information.Neon can also act as an orchestrator in Google Antigravity, directing parallel Hydrogen subagents to handle different parts of a task. The model shares progress during long sessions and is designed to maintain performance as workflows become more complicated.Beyond coding, Google is positioning Neon for enterprise analysis and scientific research. Its 1-million-token context window allows it to process large volumes of information across spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video.The model ranked first on several reported evaluations, including the Legal Research Bench, Tax Agent Bench and Zapier’s AutomationBench. It also achieved 70.5 percent on Terminal-Bench Science and 84 percent on RiemannBench, which tests mathematical reasoning.Lower costs and stronger securityGoogle is also highlighting Neon’s pricing and cybersecurity capabilities. The model costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Cached input tokens cost $0.15 per million, representing a 95 percent discount.At its default high thinking level, Google said Neon delivered a 32 percent lower cost per task than Carbon. The company also reported cost savings of roughly 50 percent to 80 percent against leading competing models on selected evaluations.For cybersecurity, a specialized Neon version is designed to help defenders identify vulnerabilities, validate risks, and patch weaknesses in software. It scored 90.5 percent on SEC-bench Pro and 76 percent on the hard tier of AutoBaxBench, according to Google.Access to this cybersecurity version will initially be limited to trusted defenders through Google’s Fairwind Program.Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business. title: Raytheon taps Ursa Major, Avio to shore up Tomahawk missile supply
content: RTX subsidiary Raytheon is widening the industrial base behind its Tomahawk cruise missiles, bringing two US propulsion companies on board to develop a new solid rocket motor booster.The American aerospace and defense firm has awarded Ursa Major and Avio USA a joint contract to design, develop and qualify the booster for the Raytheon-produced missile. The multi-year agreement could establish both companies as additional qualified US suppliers, expanding domestic manufacturing options for a critical US Navy weapon.The partnership comes as the US defense industry seeks to strengthen its ability to manufacture critical munitions and reduce vulnerabilities in its supply chains.Ursa Major and Avio USA will combine their respective expertise in solid rocket propulsion, advanced manufacturing, and production. Avio brings experience in solid rocket motor development and manufacturing, while Ursa Major contributes its propulsion design capabilities and advanced manufacturing processes.The companies aim to qualify the jointly developed booster and establish their eligibility for future production orders. The announcement does not confirm that either company has received a production contract.Expanding domestic productionThe agreement also supports Avio USA’s plans to expand its manufacturing footprint in the country. The company broke ground on a new advanced solid rocket motor manufacturing facility in southern Virginia in September.The facility is intended to strengthen domestic production capabilities and support the company’s growing presence in the US defence industry.For Ursa Major, the partnership adds to its expanding solid rocket motor portfolio and manufacturing investments. The Colorado-based company develops propulsion systems for multiple tactical missile programmes, alongside hypersonic weapons and space mobility systems.The collaboration is designed to give Raytheon additional sourcing options for a critical missile component while encouraging competition among suppliers.“By dual-sourcing this critical component with both Avio USA and Ursa Major, we’re strengthening our supply chain, encouraging innovation, and building the capacity needed to meet the Navy’s mission requirements well into the future,” said Sam Deneke, president of Naval Power at Raytheon.Strengthening missile supply chainsThe Tomahawk is a long-range cruise missile used by the US Navy to strike targets at extended distances. Its propulsion system is central to the missile’s ability to reach targets during missions.Expanding the pool of qualified booster suppliers could help Raytheon improve production flexibility and reduce reliance on a limited number of sources for critical components.The initiative also reflects a wider effort to expand the US defense industrial base as military demand for precision-guided weapons and other munitions grows.Avio USA CEO James Syring said the award marked an important step for the company’s planned US manufacturing facility and its role in the domestic defense supply chain.Ursa Major president Jason Meredith said the partnership would create additional reliable sources of solid rocket motors for Raytheon and the US Navy.However, the companies must first complete the design, development and qualification process before becoming eligible for future production orders.The announcement therefore represents an expansion of the Tomahawk program’s potential supplier base rather than an immediate increase in missile output.

title: How many chapters and missions in GTA 6? Full campaign and cheat guide
content: Grand Theft Auto 6 packs a lengthy single-player campaign into five story chapters. Players follow Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos through a sprawling criminal adventure across the fictional state of Leonida. The campaign features more than 90 main story missions, making it considerably larger than GTA 5’s 74-mission storyline.Rockstar Games has structured the adventure around its two protagonists and their growing criminal partnership. Players will progress through different stages of their journey, with each chapter introducing new challenges and opportunities. The story takes players across different parts of Leonida, including the sprawling streets of Vice City and its surrounding regions. The campaign also gives players opportunities to experience the criminal underworld from both protagonists’ perspectives.Spoiler-free guide: Here’s how the campaign breaks down, how long players can expect to spend completing it, and what they should know before starting. GTA 6 has five chaptersGTA 6 begins with a Prologue before moving into five main story chapters. The first chapter, Just Like Paradise, contains 22 missions. Chapter 2, titled Paradise Lost, follows with 11 missions and introduces further developments in Jason and Lucia’s criminal journey.Chapter 3, Ti** A** Drug Money, features 26 missions, making it the longest section of the campaign. Chapter 4, Vice City, Baby, comes close with another 25 missions. The final chapter, Top of the World, Ma, wraps up the story across seven missions.Jason and Lucia in GTA 6. Credit – Rockstar GamesTogether, these chapters account for 91 main story missions. Some mission guides report a higher total of 93 entries. That difference comes from counting additional mandatory story activities separately. Consequently, the overall number can vary depending on how individual guides classify these activities.Chapters 3 and 4 alone account for 51 missions. Players will therefore spend a substantial portion of their playthrough progressing through these sections before reaching the final chapter.How long is GTA 6?Completing the main campaign requires a substantial time commitment. GameSpot estimates that players will need upwards of 65 hours to finish the central storyline. That figure can climb considerably for players who explore Leonida and pursue optional activities.Some GTA 6 reviews mention spending between 90 and 100 hours during their playthroughs. Those additional hours included exploring the game’s wider collection of activities. Reaching 100 percent completion could require upwards of 200 hours, according to the publication’s estimates.Players who focus exclusively on the main objectives will still need several dozen hours. Those who enjoy discovering hidden locations, completing side activities, and exploring the map can expect a considerably longer experience.What to know before playingGTA 6 also changes several familiar aspects of Rockstar’s mission structure. The game drops the Gold Medal objectives found in previous installments. Players no longer need to complete specific challenges involving accuracy or mission completion times.Jason and Lucia in GTA 6. Credit – Rockstar GamesMission replay also works differently. Players cannot revisit completed missions through a dedicated replay menu. Keeping manual save files provides a useful alternative for returning to important sections.Character switching becomes another important gameplay feature. Starting with the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, players can switch between Jason and Lucia during missions. Holding Right on the D-pad activates this feature.Does GTA 6 have cheat codes?According to GTA Base, GTA 6 reportedly features 61 cheat codes. Players may need to complete the main story before accessing them. The reported system also includes additional unlock requirements for certain cheats. For example, the $250,000 money cheat unlocks after completing the story. Players must complete 100 workouts to unlock the Body Armor cheat, while winning 25 silver medals at Shooting Ranges unlocks Infinite Ammo.With five chapters and more than 90 main story missions, Rockstar Games’ GTA 6 offers a lengthy adventure. Players can expect dozens of hours of criminal escapades before the story reaches its conclusion.

title: US tests 56-year-old Minuteman III as Sentinel successor looms
content: The unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) flew from California to a test range in the Marshall Islands as the Air Force gathered data for the missile’s remaining service life before Sentinel entered service.The US Air Force has successfully conducted another operational test of its aging LGM-30G Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), validating the reliability of the country’s land-based nuclear deterrent as it prepares for a generational transition to the next-generation LGM-35A Sentinel.The launch, designated GT-257, lifted off Tuesday, from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California and involved an unarmed Minuteman III missile. Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) stressed that the test was scheduled years in advance and not related to ongoing geopolitical events, a standard message accompanying routine ICBM evaluations.Test of weapon system, personnelAccording to the Air Force, the launch served as a comprehensive evaluation of both the weapon system and the personnel responsible for operating and sustaining America’s land-based nuclear force. Engineers monitored the missile throughout its flight, collecting data on propulsion, guidance, flight performance, and reentry to support sustainment, engineering, and lifecycle management of the nearly six-decade-old system.“The ability to conduct these rigorous, realistic tests relies on the dedication of our Airmen and is foundational to ensuring the safety and surety of the Minuteman system,” Air Force Global Strike Command Commander Gen. S.L. Davis said in a statement. The command noted it has now completed more than 300 Minuteman III test launches since the program began.Ahead of the launch, authorities issued navigational warnings for areas extending across the Pacific Ocean, with local officials in California advising residents that the nighttime launch from Vandenberg could be visible across much of the Central Coast. As with previous tests, the missile was expected to travel roughly 4,200 miles (6,760 km) to the Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site at Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands.Backbone of US nuclear triadFirst deployed in 1970, the Minuteman III remains the land-based leg of the US nuclear triad, complementing submarine-launched ballistic missiles and strategic bombers. The current force consists of 400 operational missiles distributed across underground silos at F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming, Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, and Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota. Missile combat crews remain on alert around the clock from hardened underground launch control centers.Although originally designed during the Cold War, the Minuteman III has undergone repeated modernization programs covering propulsion, guidance systems, command electronics, and reentry vehicles to keep the missile operational well beyond its intended service life. Routine flight tests allow engineers to verify that those upgrades continue to perform as expected while generating data for future maintenance decisions.The latest launch comes as the Pentagon continues development of the LGM-35A Sentinel, which will eventually replace the Minuteman III fleet. Until the new missile is fielded, the Air Force said routine tests such as GT-257 remain essential to ensuring the aging ICBM force continues to provide a safe, secure, and credible strategic deterrent.

title: Giant electric ferries to carry 1,500 travelers, 500 cars at 40 knots
content: Three colossal electric ferries will be fitted with some of the world’s largest lithium iron phosphate (LFP) marine batteries, which will have a combined energy storage capacity of 165 megawatt-hours (MWh).The batteries will be supplied by AYK Energy, a marine battery manufacturer, for Danish ferry operator Molslinjen. The company has secured what it describes as the largest battery contract in ferry history.Each vessel will feature a 55 MWh DNV type-approved Polaris battery. The ferries will carry up to 1,500 passengers and 500 vehicles each, reach speeds of up to 40 knots (46 miles per hour), and support high-capacity charging in just 30 minutes.At the moment, the three fully electric catamarans are under construction at Incat Tasmania in Australia. Once delivered, they will become Europe’s largest electric ferries. “AYK is immensely proud to provide our new Polaris battery systems for these,” Chris Kruger, AYK Energy’s founder, pointed out. More power, less weightAccording to Kruger, the original batteries weighed over 772 US tons (700 tonnes) each. However, their engineers managed to reduce the weight to less than 441 US tons (400 tonnes). “We decided to rethink the battery’s design from the ground up to reduce weight and improve performance,” he revealed. This represents a reduction of more than 331 US tons (300 tonnes), which was a decisive factor in securing the contract.The company achieved this by using new battery cells, manufacturing techniques inspired by the automotive industry, as well as a lighter aluminum structure. The batteries rely on LFP chemistry for greater safety.“This is not a car where the driver can simply step out onto the road if there is a fire,” Kruger noted. “This is the reason AYK secured the first type approval of LFP battery technology, which is considerably safer than the previously used NMC chemistry.”Meanwhile, Carsten Jensen, Molslinjen’s CEO highlighted that battery weight was crucial because the vessels must travel at high speeds across Denmark’s Kattegat. “This provides a proven level of safety that is on a par with, or probably even better than, what we have with diesel today,” he added. Electric ferries for DenmarkThe three new ferries will operate between Jutland and Zealand. They will use fully electric systems instead of conventional propulsion. AYK Energy will provide the DNV type-approved Polaris batteries through an agreement with Wärtsilä, which will provide the integrated electric propulsion systems and waterjets.“The speed how AYK is bringing latest LFP technologies into the marine industry is impressive,” Torsten Büssow, PhD, Director of Electrical Integration at Wärtsilä, said in a press release. “For large ferries we have to find a balance between short high power charging and long high energy sailing times combined with a weight challenge on aluminum catamarans like these.”The first vessel is expected to arrive in Denmark in late 2027 and enter service in the first quarter of 2028. The remaining two are scheduled to arrive in 2028 and 2029.Meanwhile, the initiative also strengthens AYK Energy’s presence in the shipping market. The company has previously supplied two 12 MWh batteries for Brittany Ferries’ hybrid-electric vessels, Guillaume de Normandie and Saint-Malo. It also delivered a six MWh battery for Svitzer’s battery-methanol tug and secured an agreement to supply Germany’s new polar research vessel, Polarstern.

title: Scientists turn old university lift into a gravity-powered messenger
content: In a surprising experiment, researchers successfully transmitted a message through a solid brick wall using gravity. No Wi-Fi routers or radio antennas were involved in this bizarre setup.Physicists at the University of Queensland (UQ) recently pulled off this feat inside their Parnell Building, proving that gravity itself can carry data. Working with a vintage 1950s elevator, the team sent the lift repeatedly between two floors. Each movement shifted a massive 1.8-tonne counterweight between specific positions representing binary zeros and ones. Meanwhile, a highly sensitive gravimeter stationed in an adjacent restroom picked up those minuscule shifts in the local gravitational field and translated the code into a single, fitting word: “Gravity.”A gravimeter is an ultra-sensitive scientific instrument designed to measure tiny variations in the Earth’s gravitational field. Geophysicists typically deploy these devices in the field to locate hidden oil reserves, monitor shifting volcanic magma, or map melting polar ice sheets. Using such specialized geological equipment to decode text messages inside a university bathroom marks a highly unusual twist on its standard day job.“It took more than 100 years to go from the first telegraph system to the mobile phone, so while gravity communication is not practical today, it could be in the future,” said Professor Andrew White. Matthew Davis, Charles Woffiden and Andrew White inside the elevator they used to send a message. Credit: The University of QueenslandNo signal, no problemStandard wireless signals like radio waves and Wi-Fi easily bounce off or get absorbed by dense obstacles, leaving commuters frustrated in tunnels and basements. Gravitational fields ignore physical barriers entirely.“Unlike the electromagnetic signals used in modern wireless communication, a gravitational signal cannot simply be screened out by placing ordinary material in its path,” explained Dr. Charles Woffinden from UQ’s School of Mathematics and Physics. “While the present system is far from practical, it demonstrates the possibility of communicating using a method that ordinary physical barriers cannot block.”Curiously, the experiment began as a completely different project. Dr. Andrew Groszek and his colleagues were initially trying to design a contactless weighbridge that could measure the mass of heavy trucks simply by reading their tiny gravitational pull. Once the team realized they could accurately detect moving mass from a distance, the leap to encoding and transmitting actual data became clear.Just a beginningDon’t expect gravity-powered internet on your smartphone anytime soon, though. Operating on a slow 1950s lift meant the system transmitted data at a glacial pace of just one bit per minute, requiring a full hour to spell out that single seven-letter word. Professor White noted that scaling up the technology depends entirely on moving larger masses faster and building more sensitive detectors. He compared the experiment to the earliest days of the telegraph, pointing out that it took over a century to evolve from clunky wires to modern mobile phones.After publishing their findings in Science Advances, the team is already looking to quantum technology to speed things up. Modeling from Professor Matthew Davis suggests that next-generation quantum gravity sensors could eventually push communication ranges to 500 meters at speeds around 15 bits per minute.While still slow by modern standards, such a system could prove invaluable in extreme environments, like deep underground mines or underwater, where conventional signals simply cannot penetrate.

title: US nuclear reactors get boost as new cloud tools slash planning delays
content: Constructing a new commercial nuclear power plant is not a piece of cake. It involves rigorous efforts, including years of exhaustive paperwork long before a single shovel hits the dirt. Companies looking to build a nuclear plant first need to evaluate sites, followed by strict compliance with regulatory approvals, and, most importantly, select the right reactor technology. They also face complex technical planning before construction can begin. Now, US nuclear developer Elementl Power is teaming up with Google Cloud to tackle those preconstruction delays using artificial intelligence. The partnership centers on Elementl Lattice, an integrated project delivery and capital management platform built on Google’s BigQuery data analytics and Gemini for business models. The system pairs cloud computing with Elementl’s experience in nuclear engineering and energy finance. Together, these capabilities replace fragmented, manual planning with standardized digital workflows. As teams use the software, Lattice captures real-world operational data to improve cost and schedule certainty across future builds.“A major preconstruction bottleneck for nuclear energy stems from an intelligence and data orchestration problem, which Elementl is using Gemini for business to tackle head-on,” said Raiford Smith, global director of Power & Energy at Google Cloud. Smith added that the technology shifts the industry away from isolated studies toward “real-time, predictive project delivery that accelerates the arrival of efficient baseload power to the grid.”Accelerating siting for upcoming projectsThe push for faster deployment is underscored by Elementl’s active infrastructure pipeline. Earlier in June, the independent developer announced plans to build a 1.5-gigawatt nuclear facility in Southeast Ohio. Through an Early Works Agreement with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy, the site will deploy BWRX-300 small modular reactors. This contract positions the installation among the earliest commercial projects of its kind in the United States.To support this growing portfolio, Elementl has already launched the first operational tool within the Lattice suite, known as Atlas. Choosing a viable nuclear site requires cross-referencing hundreds of geographic, environmental, and grid-infrastructure variables. Atlas evaluates several candidate locations across thousands of square miles at the same time, factoring in the specific technical demands of multiple reactor designs. Preliminary desktop research that once took months can now be completed in days or weeks. As a result, engineering teams can move into deeper physical site assessments much faster.Standardizing designs for scalable deploymentFuture updates to Lattice will target another major source of nuclear delays: regulatory duplication. Engineers are developing a unified digital ledger to track a plant’s approved design specifications, licensing requirements, and structural modifications. Maintaining this controlled master record will allow teams to reuse verified regulatory and engineering work across subsequent plants built with standardized reactor designs.Elementl Chairman and CEO Chris Colbert said the collaboration turns institutional nuclear expertise into practical software that helps teams “move faster and with greater confidence.”The platform cuts down on repetitive engineering tasks and carries lessons from one project into the next. Ultimately, this approach makes commercial nuclear deployment both repeatable and scalable.

title: US firm's tool unlocks 10 times more simulations for aircraft design
content: U.S.-based aviation and logistics startup Poseidon Aerospace is using artificial intelligence (AI) to test and improve its autonomous cargo aircraft on a computer before it ever flies.To conduct these tests, the company is using AI tools developed by Flexcompute, a Boston-based physics simulation and AI company founded in 2015.The AI automatically prepares the aircraft’s digital model for aerodynamic simulations, allowing engineers to predict how it will perform in the air much faster than before.Using conventional methods, building the aircraft’s aerodynamic database—a collection of performance data used to understand how the aircraft behaves under different flight conditions—took nearly eight months.Now, that timeline has been drastically shortened. The use of AI-powered geometry preparation and simulation tools has reduced the time required to generate the database from eight months to just three weeks, the company said in a statement on Tuesday (November 17).The faster workflow also allows engineers to run 10 times more simulations, helping them refine the aircraft’s design before building and flying it.Poseidon Aerospace designs, manufactures, and operates unmanned cargo aircraft for regional freight transport and defense logistics in remote areas with limited infrastructure. Its flagship aircraft, Egret, is a 50-foot autonomous freighter capable of carrying up to 4,000 pounds (1,814 kg) of cargo while operating from short paved or unpaved runways without relying on conventional airport infrastructure.Building ‘Physics Twin’But how can the company evaluate an aircraft that hasn’t been built yet?To make that possible, Poseidon is creating a highly accurate virtual copy of the aircraft, called a “Physics Twin,” using GeometryAI and Flexcompute Flow (formerly Flow360).Instead of waiting until the real aircraft is built and flown, engineers test its performance on a computer throughout the design process.This approach is different from building a traditional digital twin that is typically used to monitor an aircraft after it has been built; a Physics Twin is created before the aircraft exists.The new method uses the laws of physics to predict how the aircraft will behave, allowing engineers to compare different designs, identify potential problems, and make improvements long before any hardware is manufactured or flight testing begins.For Poseidon, the biggest benefit isn’t just speed; it’s giving engineers more time to explore and refine new aircraft designs.“With a small engineering team, we want AI to expand what our engineers can explore, not add complexity,” said Rohan Sharma, Ph.D., vice president of engineering at Poseidon Aerospace.“GeometryAI gets our aircraft geometry ready for simulation, Flexcompute Flow gives us answers quickly, and our internal Python workflow with an AI agent connects the process end to end. The result is less time managing tools and more time engineering the aircraft, making design decisions, and closing trade studies.”According to the company, adopting the technology has accelerated parts of its engineering workflow by 25 times. Design studies that were expected to take about 200 days can now be completed in just over a week.“Regional air cargo is ripe for aircraft informed by bleeding-edge design techniques,” said Vera Yang, president of Flexcompute. “We’re removing computational bottlenecks, enabling innovators like Poseidon to ask better questions, explore more designs, and bring transformative aircraft to market demonstrably faster and safer.”

title: Indian study sees perovskites as a way around silicon wafer imports
content:
Indian study sees perovskites as a way around silicon wafer imports
A new report produced by
P3C Technology and Solutions
, in association with the Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA), argues that perovskite solar technology could let India build advanced solar manufacturing without relying on imported polysilicon, wafers and equipment, which remain a major dependence even as the country builds up domestic cell, wafer and ingot capacity.
The report, titled “Perovskite Solar: India’s Atmanirbharta Opportunity in Next Generation PV,” says perovskite manufacturing can bypass the polysilicon, ingot and wafer stages, where import dependence is highest. It estimates factory capital expenditure at 70% to 80% below that of conventional crystalline silicon lines. It also puts the potential domestic value addition at about ₹74,000 crore (about US$7.9 billion) over 15 years, though it notes that the year-by-year build-up of that estimate has not yet been published.
The report also projects that perovskite modules could lose less output in hot weather, raising the capacity utilization factor from about 20% to about 25% and cutting the levelized cost of energy by 30% to 40%. These figures are projections, and the report says they need validation with long-term field data. It notes that perovskite degradation, put at 0.5% to 1% a year against about 0.5% for silicon, reflects pilot-stage understanding rather than a bankable 25-year record.
For adoption, the report recommends starting with single-junction perovskite manufacturing, then adding silicon-perovskite tandems on India’s existing TOPCon cell base. It calls for a provisional two-tier category under India’s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) with defined stability milestones, dedicated R&D and pilot funding through the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, and independent techno-economic modeling.
“Perovskite is a promising next step that builds on this foundation,” said ISMA Secretary General Amit Manohar, referring to manufacturers’ existing investments in cells, wafers and ingots. P3C CEO and co-founder Sooraj Kumar said the company is developing its own absorber chemistry, assembly line and intellectual property in India, and that its modules are in reliability testing at the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE). P3C and NISE
signed a partnership in early 2025
to speed up perovskite market entry in India.

title: Buried-interface additive passivates both interface and bulk in perovskite solar cells
content:
Buried-interface additive passivates both interface and bulk in perovskite solar cells
Researchers at Wuhan Textile University, Anhui University, Wuhan University and Hubei Normal University have developed a buried-interface modifier that reduces defects at the bottom of the perovskite layer and inside the perovskite bulk, using a single molecule.
Image from: Nano Energy
In inverted perovskite solar cells, defects at the interface between the perovskite and the hole transport layer cause non-radiative recombination and limit efficiency. The team pre-anchored potassium 4-pyridyltrifluoroborate (PyBF
K) on the self-assembled monolayer beneath the perovskite. The PyBF
anion passivates both undercoordinated lead ions and organic cations through Lewis acid-base coordination and hydrogen bonding. The potassium ions then detach from the interface and migrate into the bulk, where they act as free interstitial passivators that lower the defect density. The researchers call this a cross-interface ion-sharing strategy, and say it also promotes oriented perovskite crystallization and improves energy-level alignment.
Buried-interface engineering has been one of the main routes to higher inverted-cell efficiency, as in a
molecular hybrid bridging approach
that reached 26.64%. Here, the modified inverted cells achieved 26.63% efficiency at 0.07 cm² and 24.24% at 1 cm², with negligible hysteresis. The devices retained 98.1% of their initial efficiency after 1,000 hours of continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1 sun.
The team also applied the strategy to a 1.67 eV wide-bandgap perovskite, reaching 23.11%, and to a 1 cm² perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell, which reached 32.2%.

title: 国家能源局有关负责同志就《关于加快推动流域水风光一体化发展的指导意见》答记者问-索比光伏网
政策分类路径: 政策 > 战略规划型政策 > 产业方向
政策分类依据: 指导意见确定流域水风光一体化重点发展方向与布局
content:
近日，国家能源局印发了《关于加快推动流域水风光一体化发展的指导意见》（国能发新能〔2026〕92号，以下简称《指导意见》）。国家能源局有关负责同志就此接受了记者采访。
问：《指导意见》出台的背景是什么？
答：流域水风光一体化发展是立足流域可再生能源资源禀赋，发挥水电灵活调节潜力，带动新能源集约高效开发利用的集成融合发展方式，是新时期水电发展的“升级版”。党中央、国务院高度重视流域水风光一体化发展工作。2024年，《中共中央国务院关于加快经济社会发展全面绿色转型的意见》提出，统筹水电开发和生态保护，推进水风光一体化开发。2026年，《中华人民共和国国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划纲要》要求，推进雅砻江、金沙江上游、澜沧江上游、藏东南（玉察）等流域水风光一体化基地建设。
为深入落实好上述部署要求，国家能源局出台《指导意见》，系统性提出加快推动流域水风光一体化发展的一揽子政策思路与举措，指导各地各有关单位统筹做好相关工作。
问：加快推动流域水风光一体化发展的总体要求是什么？
答：践行能源安全新战略，以碳达峰碳中和目标为牵引，坚持一体化资源配置、一体化规划布局、一体化开发建设、一体化联合调度、一体化市场消纳、一体化安全保障，加快推动流域水风光一体化发展，扩大优质规模化绿电供给，探索100%可再生能源新模式新业态，培育发展新质生产力，更好支撑新型能源体系和能源强国建设，服务经济社会发展全面绿色转型。
到2030年，雅砻江、金沙江上游、澜沧江上游、藏东南（玉察）等流域水风光一体化基地建设取得积极进展，形成一批促进新能源就近就地消纳的“水风光+”新业态新模式。到2035年，水风光一体化发展成为我国水电高质量升级发展的重要方式，流域水风光资源得到更高效能协同开发、更大范围优化配置、更高价值消纳利用，为经济社会高质量发展注入强劲绿色动能。
问：优化流域水风光一体化发展布局有哪些具体考虑？
答：一是以西南主要流域为主攻方向，加快推进雅砻江、金沙江上游、澜沧江上游、藏东南（玉察）等流域水风光一体化先行基地建设，扎实推进雅鲁藏布江中、下游，大渡河，金沙江中、下游等流域水风光一体化基地规划编制，深入开展其他西南主要流域水风光一体化基地规划研究论证。二是以西北主要流域为补充，扎实推进黄河上游水风光一体化基地规划编制，研究推进内陆河流水风光一体化基地规划建设，有序探索建设以抽水蓄能等为主要调节电源的新能源基地。三是兼顾其他主要流域发展。重点依托红水河等其他流域梯级水电调节能力，结合周边新能源资源禀赋和电网条件，科学推进水风光一体化发展。
问：如何全面落实流域水风光“六个一体化”发展要求？
答：一是强化一体化资源配置。根据流域水电和新能源资源匹配情况，统筹相关因素，优化流域水风光电源配置。二是坚持一体化规划布局。打破单一品类能源项目独立规划传统模式，衔接相关规划和电力主网架结构，统筹推进水风光电源一体化规划布局。三是统筹一体化开发建设。考虑不同类别电源和送出工程建设周期和开发进度，科学安排项目建设时序。同步规划建设配套电网工程，促进网源协同。四是推进一体化联合调度。加强流域梯级水风光发电联合优化调度，统筹防洪、生态、灌溉、发电、航运、安全等要求，增强水电、抽水蓄能配合新能源运行调节的能力。五是促进一体化市场消纳。健全水风光一体化市场消纳体制机制，积极推动具备条件的水风光一体化项目整体参与市场交易。六是加强一体化安全保障。支持水风光一体化项目探索构建一体化安全管理体系，全面提升安全水平和应急能力。
问：如何加快培育“水风光+”100%可再生能源新业态新模式？
答：一是探索“水风光+绿色氢氨醇”协同发展。在西南等高原地区，因地制宜探索发展绿氢、绿氨、绿氧等产业，满足工矿、农业和民生需求。在西北等具备条件地区，积极有序推动流域水风光与绿色氢氨醇耦合集成，促进高载能产业低碳转型。二是引导“水风光+绿色算力”互补支撑。挖掘已建水电站闲置地下洞室群资源潜力，发展岩洞式算力舱、智算设施等新业态新模式。大力发展适应水风光出力特性的“柔性算力”。提高水风光出力预测精准度，引导算力负荷主动避峰填谷，促进算电双向协同。三是推动“水风光+绿色产业”双向赋能。在流域水风光一体化项目所在地区，积极探索应用供电电量清晰、物理可溯源的方式，发展以新能源电量为主体、水电补充调节支撑的绿色用能产业。在流域水风光一体化项目受电地区，前瞻谋划绿色产业集聚发展，积极探索应用多年期绿电购电协议等方式，培育壮大符合转型方向、创造绿色价值、负荷弹性可控的新能源友好型产业。
问：如何做好《指导意见》组织实施？
答：《指导意见》提出，国家能源局加强全国流域水风光一体化发展工作统筹。各省级能源主管部门负责本省（区、市）范围内流域水风光一体化发展工作，涉及主要河流、通过特高压直流通道跨省跨区消纳或规划新增服务特定电源抽水蓄能的，在国家能源局指导下开展工作。国家能源局派出机构和地方能源主管部门按照职责分工，加强服务和监管。
